candidates.title: Map resume details into application forms

demandEvidence.chore: The poster spends two hours every day entering resume data into forms tailored to one or two companies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I spent two hours every day filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies.

ease.reason: A beginner could prototype form-field mapping from a supplied resume and sample form, but no implementation reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: job seekers might pay for less repetitive application entry; the discussion establishes no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can map a resume to a few manually supplied fields; company-specific forms and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed tool can prepare field values, but a person must check each form and submit it; no automation capability is documented.

evidence.reason: The fresh post states a daily two-hour resume-entry chore for forms tailored to one or two companies, but gives no field details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: assess a narrow draft of resume facts for repeated application fields; no supplied source supports live form integration or buyer willingness to pay.

candidates.title: Draft replies to Messenger text and images

demandEvidence.chore: Handle customer messages received through Facebook Messenger; the post title indicates text and image replies.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I am building a scenario in Make.com to handle customer messages received through Facebook Messenger.

ease.reason: A beginner can test reply drafts from sample text and manually described images, but no supplied reference documents message or image handling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service businesses handling Messenger inquiries might pay for draft assistance; this post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can accept sample messages and manual image descriptions, draft a reply, and test human review; live Messenger access is unsupported.

autonomy.reason: The proposed test drafts from operator-supplied inputs; a person must describe images, check context and approve every reply, with no integration evidence.

evidence.reason: The post says its author is building a Make scenario for customer messages through Facebook Messenger; the title indicates text and image replies, but details are limited.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a narrow student test can draft replies from supplied text and manually described images, but live Messenger integration and recurring buyer demand are unproved.
